about: Synthetic labelled cases for the JEV-1 offline eval. Every request, result, claim and evidence string below was written for this file. No customer, tester or Discord data appears anywhere, and no real person is named. Retail chain names are used only as generic stand-ins for named stores. Question definitions live in scripts/jev-eval.mjs and follow docs/JEV-1.md.

judgments.1: Request interpretation. State is {request, workspace_location}. Questions: scope (choice), names_stores, names_location, names_quantity, substitutes_ok (nouls).
judgments.2: Result sufficiency and next step. State is {constraints, tool_used, results}. Questions: satisfies (choice), one noul per rung (can_answer_now, answerable_now, needs_more_sources, needs_page_fetch, needs_tinyfish, needs_desktop_browser), one noul per entry of constraints.stores_named keyed has_result_<slug>. Jev never orders the rungs. Code holds the order answer_now, search_more_sources, fetch_pages, tinyfish, desktop_browser and picks the cheapest rung whose noul is at or above 0.6. Each judgment 2 case carries cheapest_rung, the rung that order picks from the labelled nouls, which is what the code-picked rung is scored against.
judgments.3: Claim check. State is {claim, evidence, sources_checked, sources_named_in_request}. Questions: support (choice), is_universal_negative (noul).
judgments.2b: Constraint confirmation, one result at a time. State is {constraints, result}. Questions: confirms_item, confirms_pack_size, confirms_store, confirms_stock_for_location, one noul each, all asked about `result.title`, `result.snippet` and `result.source` by path. expected.required is the subset the constraints make required: item and stock always, pack size only when constraints.pack_sizes is non-empty, store only when constraints.stores_named is non-empty. expected.fetch is true when any required confirmation is false. Code decides fetch when any required noul is under 0.6, and derives the required set from the constraints rather than reading the label.

store_slug_rule: lowercase, then every run of characters outside a-z0-9 becomes a single underscore, then trim underscores. Home Depot becomes home_depot, Lowe's becomes lowe_s, Best Buy becomes best_buy.

cases.code_rule: Jev misses this one: it answers supports, at confidence 0.36, with is_universal_negative 0.82. The plan's code rule catches it. A universal negative whose support answer is supports below 0.6 confidence is read as no_evidence, so the claim lands on the is_universal_negative >= 0.7 and support is not supports branch and is returned to the model as an unsupported claim to soften. The same rule fires on no other case in this file: every claim scoped to the sources checked answers is_universal_negative at 0.05 or below, so nothing correct is dragged in with it.

label_corrections.why: The scope criteria allow an implied place and the state supplies one in workspace_location, so local_in_store is the right reading of this state. The original label read the request field alone, which is not what the scope question is asked about.
